newsitem.title: USA: Republicans cut King bit from affirmative action ad.
newsitem.headline: Republicans cut King bit from affirmative action ad.

text.p: The California Republican Party said on Thursday it would delete a clip using a famous speech by Dr. Martin Luther King from a commercial against affirmative action after his estate complained.
State Republican Party Chairman John Herrington said the makers of the political ad were re-editing it and would cut out a fragment of the slain civil rights leader's "I have a dream speech."

The state's Republican Party caused a furore this week when word leaked out that it planned to use part of the King speech in a commercial supporting Proposition 209, which would ban state affirmative action programmes based on race or sex.

Several civil rights leaders condemned the use of King's words in the ad, saying King supported affirmative action. The company that manages the King estate asked the makers of the spot not to use King's words or image.

Phillip Jones, president of Atlanta-based Intellectual Properties Management Inc., said the company did not allow King's copyrighted speeches to be used in partisan commercials. "We don't feel it's appropriate. We've always had this policy," Jones said.
The controversial ad was due to be launched on Wednesday but the Republican Party stopped its release because of the outcry.
Republican officials made clear they had decided to cut the King section to avoid the possibility of legal action.
"Frankly, we are not in the business of litigation. I do not think it will be the best use of our time and our money," Herrington told a news conference in Sacramento.

The original ad featured an eight-second excerpt from King's 1963 speech in which he said he dreamed of a society where people "will not be judged by the colour of their skin but the content of their character."
It is replaced in the new version by an announcer's voice saying: "We should be judged on merit, not by gender or the colour of our skin." The new ads were expected to air in California on Friday.

Herrington said the Republican Party planned to spend more than $2 million on ads supporting Proposition 209. Californians were due to vote on Nov. 5 on the controversial measure, which would roll back affirmative action programmes used since the 1960s to increase opportunities for women and racial minorities.
